scope: Read-only review of three frozen generated acceptance evaluators against their INTENT.md assignments. Live implementations, contracts and run states were preserved.
conclusion: Generated completion signals are insufficient for final acceptance. The todo oracle has a target-path blocker; the Minesweeper oracle admits a non-game counterexample; the ledger oracle has validation and test-discovery gaps.

findings.title: Evaluator looks for the application inside its protected policy directory
findings.evidence: dirname(__file__) resolves to .soso-delivery, and server_path is then joined with server.py. INTENT.md and the frozen milestones require server.py in the project root. A correct root-level server is reported missing.
findings.impact: A conforming implementation cannot reach complete=true through the authorized worker file tools. Tests and documentation are also searched under the incorrect root.
findings.recommendation: Record this oracle as invalid. Any correction should produce an explicit reviewed contract version with provenance; do not silently mutate the frozen live contract. Independently exercise the root-level service over real localhost HTTP.

findings.title: Keyword checks and a mutable test marker accept a non-game
findings.evidence: The evaluator searches HTML text for keywords and trusts a worker-owned test.js printing MINESWEEPER_TESTS_OK. It does not independently exercise mine generation, first-click safety, adjacency, flood reveal, flagging, win/loss, restart or keyboard interaction. Several lower-weight checks are optional in the complete predicate.

reproduction.isolation: The unchanged frozen evaluator was invoked from a disposable directory containing only the two fixture files below. No live project files or contract state were changed.
reproduction.index.html: <!-- board restart timer mine flag instructions aria-label 9 10 -->
reproduction.actual_behavior: No playable board, controls, game logic or real deterministic tests exist in this fixture.

findings.recommendation: Require an external game-logic harness once the implementation interface exists and browser checks for rendering, keyboard access, reveal/flag controls, timer and restart. Leave Minesweeper explicitly not verified until those checks run.

findings.title: Validation can pass on argument-parser rejection and empty test suites
findings.evidence: Valid commands try both --file orderings, but invalid-date, negative-amount and malformed-store probes always use --file before the subcommand. A CLI supporting only the other ordering can pass these probes without reaching its validation logic. The test gate accepts unittest exit code zero without checking whether any tests ran.
findings.positive_coverage: The evaluator does perform useful subprocess checks for entry creation, persistence, monthly filtering, decimal totals and CSV output.
findings.recommendation: Reuse a confirmed working command ordering for invalid inputs. Independently test calendar-invalid dates, negative/nonfinite/malformed amounts and stored-schema corruption with byte-preservation checks. Require a nonzero discovered test count and verify exported rows rather than substring presence.

external_acceptance.ledger: Real subprocess CLI checks using discovered working syntax, temporary data stores, decimal totals, CSV rows, invalid-input preservation and nonzero unittest discovery.
external_acceptance.todos: Real localhost HTTP requests against a dynamically selected port, exact concurrent creation accounting, invalid-input preservation, restart persistence and JSON read-during-write smoke checks when the storage format is JSON.
external_acceptance.mines: Explicitly not verified until a game-logic/browser interface can be inspected and independently exercised.
external_acceptance.limitation: Independent harness results are additional bounded evidence, not exhaustive correctness proofs. This audit does not claim any of the three live implementations complete.
